lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Estimate then describe how you would measure the height of a classroom door.

FEEDBACK
Estimate around 2 m; measure with a tape/metre stick from floor to top.

WATCH FOR
Skipping the estimate removes a sense check for reading the scale wrong.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Estimate and measure (or plan measures for) ten lengths. Record estimate, measure and close/far for each.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Estimate a desk ≈ 70 cm; measure 68 cm — close. An estimate of 7 m for a desk is unreasonable.

TRY FIRST
Estimate then describe how you would measure the height of a classroom door.

FEEDBACK
Estimate around 2 m; measure with a tape/metre stick from floor to top.
teach_steps.explain:
Estimating length uses benchmarks (hand span, metre stick) then measuring checks the estimate.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Skipping the estimate removes a sense check for reading the scale wrong. Correct the value or method, not just the appearance of the digits.
